newsitem.title: USA: Dow halts two-session slide but tech stocks tumble.
newsitem.headline: Dow halts two-session slide but tech stocks tumble.

text.p: The Dow industrials halted a steep two-session slide on Monday after a rebound in the bond market soothed investor worries over rising long-term interest rates.
The Dow industrials finished up about 31 points, or 0.4 percent, at 8062 in a late session rally after being off as many as 67 points.
The blue chip index had lost 228 points in the previous two sessions amid a sharp rise in long-term rates.
But the late-session recovery did not spread fully across all sectors, with the Nasdaq composite finishing off about 12 points at 1587 due to extended profit-taking in high technology stocks.
Losing issues also edged gainers by a 14-to-13 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange.
Despite the mixed performance, market players said they did not see much of a carryover from Friday's 157-point Dow sell-off. Several said trading was quite, typical of a summer Monday.
NYSE volume was mild at about 482 million shares.
"We really didn't get much of a follow-through to that scare on Friday," said Bill Allyn, head of trading at Jefferies and Co. "That in itself is good news."

As they did last week, stocks keyed of bonds on Monday. The rebound in blue chips was triggered after bonds responded to remarks on a newswire in which Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillps suggested there was no immediate need for a credit tightening.
Recent economic data hinting at a strengthening U.S. economy have rekindled market speculation that the Fed will need to raise interest rates to keep inflation at bay.
The 30-year Treasury bond was flat in late trading, its yield at 6.64. The yield fell back after rising as high as 6.69 percent, the highest since the closing level on July 2.
Market players said they expected tentative trading until Wednesday's report on retail sales and July wholesale inflation. Thursday brings a report on retail inflation.
Investors be looking for any hints in the data of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
"Don't expect it to get much clearer until Wednesday and Thursday," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management. "Then we'll see where we go from there."
The firm bond market helped recently battered financial
stocks, which are sensitive to shifts in interest rates. American Express Co rose 1-12/16 to 82-3/16, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 2-12/16 to 113-7/16 and Citicorp rose 2-1/4 to 136-1/4.

Pharmaceutical stocks slipped. Morgan Stanley lowered its recommended portfolio weighting of the drug sector, saying recent increased industry spending reduced chances of near-term upside earnings surprises. Warner-Lambert Co fell 3-7/8 to 132-1/4, Merck & Co Inc lost 3-9/16 to 95-1/4 and Eli Lilly and Co dropped four to 108-11/16.
Hershey Foods Corp rose 4-7/8 to 57-3/8 boosted by an upgrade from Morgan Stanley.

Publisher Reader's Digest Association Inc rose 3-3/8 to 28-1/4 after saying its chairman and chief executive officer, James Schadt, had resigned. The move came one month after the company slashed its dividend and earnings forecast.

Shares of CSG Systems International Inc rose 3-1/4 to 26-3/8 after it signed two major agreements with a Tele-Communications Inc affiliate. Its rival USCS International Inc fell 10-7/8 to 20-1/8 on the news. Both firms offer customer management products and services.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.46 points to 937.00.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 11.78 to 1586.74.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
